understanding.emotion: pulled in every direction and empty
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call a mind that won't settle, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from a mind that runs in every direction to one that can rest long enough to hear what it itself needs.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the restlessness and the exhaustion, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the mind has become its own enemy by being fed every demand and never asked what it needs.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the one who stays the same in the middle does not let the mind become its own enemy.
week_beats.act: You try withdrawing the mind for a few minutes and asking yourself what you need before answering anyone else.
week_beats.story: A man who built his family's future without building his own shows you what happens when the mind is never asked what it needs.

understanding.core_struggle: A man in midlife is pulled between his wife's wish to return, his family's rising needs, and a mind that will not settle because he cannot name what he himself needs.
understanding.mirror: You send money home for eleven years, and now everyone needs something from you, and you still cannot name what you need.
understanding.insight: It is not the money or the family that keeps you up. It is the mind that has never been asked what it needs, and so it runs in every direction at once.

queries.hook: A mind that will not settle because it is being pulled in every direction, and the exhaustion of not knowing what you yourself need. My parents are getting older far away.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy, and it feeds on every demand it is given.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, need and duty, come and go; the one who stays the same in the middle is the one who does not let the mind become its own enemy.
queries.act: Practise withdrawing the mind for even a few minutes each day; let the day's duties go before sleep, and ask yourself what you need before you answer anyone else.
queries.story: A man who spent years sending money home and never stopped to ask himself what he was building, until the day he had to choose between his wife and his family.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless, turbulent, and powerful. He says it is as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees with him. He says that practice and letting go are what train the mind, so it can be steadied.
verse.for_you: You are pulled in every direction and feel empty. The mind runs in every direction because it has never been asked what it needs. Today, just notice where the mind races without trying to stop it.

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.meaning: Years ago, two childhood friends, Bhasa and Vilasa, grew up together in a forest hermitage. They later drifted apart and spent decades in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, Bhasa asks if Vilasa has found peace. Vilasa admits he has not, because the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries. This verse shows that a mind caught in the loop of past actions and future duties, never pausing to ask what it itself needs, becomes its own enemy.
verse.for_you: The mind has become its own enemy by being fed every demand and never asked what it needs. Today, the lists of work and family are not the enemy, but the fact that your mind is never allowed to simply be. Let the mind faint for a moment.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: In the long closing chapter on peace, Ashtavakra paints the calm of the wise.
verse.sanskrit: अकुर्वन्नपि सङ्क्षोभाद् व्यग्रः सर्वत्र मूढधीः । कुर्वन्नपि तु कृत्यानि कुशलो हि निराकुलः ॥
verse.line: A restless mind is agitated even doing nothing; a skilled one stays calm doing everything.
verse.translation: The fool is restless even when doing nothing; the skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing.
verse.why: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

prasang.title: The calm of the wise
prasang.summary: In a hundred verses Ashtavakra paints the inner peace of the wise: calm while busy, unmoved by gain or loss, praise or blame, at ease whether in the city or the forest. The restless, by contrast, chase peace and never find it.
prasang.lesson: Calm isn't found by chasing it or changing places; it is how you hold ordinary life.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, the king who has already given up his throne to seek truth. The king sits in the quiet of a forest, having left behind every duty that once defined him. Ashtavakra tells him that a restless mind is agitated even when doing nothing. The fool is restless even when doing nothing. The skilful one stays calm even when doing everything that needs doing. The point is that calm is not found by chasing it or changing places. It is how you hold ordinary life.
verse.for_you: The lists of what you could do never end. The mind runs even in the silence. Let the body do its work, but do not let the mind become its own enemy. It is enough to be doing. Let the doing be enough.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that a person can be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. This is how a free person lives. They let go of what is lost and take up what comes. They do the work at hand and speak gently. They move through the world with a clear mind, treating the whole world as family.
verse.for_you: You are doing the work at hand, but your mind is racing. You can be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Let your hands keep moving while your mind finds its own pace.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
verse.line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
verse.translation: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna is showing Arjuna how to sit with the mind when it will not stay still. He says that the mind will wander. It will run after its own noise. The instruction is not to fight it or to give up. It is to gently guide it back. You do this over and over. Each time you notice it has left, you bring it back to the self. That is the work. It is a quiet, patient return, not a single victory.
verse.for_you: Before you answer anyone today, let your hand rest on your desk and ask your mind one quiet question. What do you need right now. Listen for the answer, and let that be your first step.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to his own mind. He asks why it exhausts itself pleasing others, replaying the past and scripting the future. The mind is told to rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. He will enjoy the pleasures that come unlooked-for. The idea is to stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes. The calm you want is already inside. The poet asks what all our gains amount to. This is not an argument against planning. It is for the worry loop once you have done your part.
verse.for_you: You are answering to everyone else. Try this today. Sit for two minutes and ask your mind what it needs before you pick up the phone. Do not plan or replay. Just let the answer come.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

script: You are pulled in every direction and feel empty. You have spent years sending money from Dubai to keep your family safe and your father healthy, and now your wife wants to come home. You are caring for your parents, and you feel the weight of it all, but the thing that exhausts you most is inside your own head.
Arjuna says this to Krishna on a battlefield, when he is overwhelmed and his mind will not stop moving. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

This is easier said than done, because the mind is not a machine you can simply switch off. When you are pulled between your wife's wish to return, your family's needs, and your work, the mind races to solve everything at once. But the texts say that holding the mind is not about forcing it to be still. It is about practice and letting go. The mind will not settle until you stop trying to hold every direction at once.
Today, just notice where the mind races without trying to stop it. You do not need to name what you need right now. Just watch the mind move. Let it run where it runs.
What does the mind run toward when you are not holding it?

depth.life: You are on the phone for hours, sending money from Dubai, while your mind runs through your parents' health, your sibling's wedding, and your wife's wish to return home. You feel pulled in every direction and empty, with no space to ask what you yourself need.
depth.points: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. It runs in every direction because it has never been asked what it needs. It is not the family or the work that keeps you up. It is the mind that will not settle.
depth.practice: Notice where your mind races today without trying to stop it.
depth.question: Where does your mind go when you are not holding the phone?
